scope: bottleneck ranking (runtime, delivery, decisions, release+migration) over existing r2/r3-A review output; re-checked, not new evidence except where noted

runtime.area: subagent large-output protection (ADR-0016 case B, Claude Code)
runtime.claim: ADR-0016 plans Case B (PreToolUse allow + updatedInput.command rewrite) as the default Bash truncation path on Claude Code. Claude Code does not honor updatedInput.command under permissionDecision:allow — the original command runs unmodified — so case B is a silent no-op: the full, untruncated output still reaches the subagent, breaking the ADR-0016 MUST ("large output never enters any subagent context").
runtime.evidence: ADR-0016.md:27 names case B as the Claude Code mechanism with no caveat.

archaeology.introduced_by: 4bc292fc (fix(hooks): claude-code Bash modify -> deny (CC ignores updatedInput.command)), Mert Koseoglu, 2026-05-31
archaeology.original_intent: "CC v2.1.x Bash tool ignores updatedInput.command substitution under permissionDecision: allow -- the original command runs unchanged... Every bun-installed Claude Code user had been silently losing the context-saving intervention since #738 shipped -- high-impact regression."
archaeology.regression_risk: v2 re-ships exactly the behaviour 4bc292fc fixed: allow+rewrite on Claude Code Bash is a no-op, so large tool output flows straight into subagent context again, on the agent that is the primary dev surface.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Case C (deny + re-issue narrower command) or a hard deny must be the Claude Code default for Bash until a live run on the pinned CC version proves case B works; any future case-B reconsideration needs its own forced-deny probe, not an assumption.

runtime.fix: Make case C/deny the Claude Code default per ADR-0016:27 fix already proposed in REVIEW-r2.md; add a CI probe repeating the 4bc292fc forced-deny check against the pinned CC version before any case-B path ships.

runtime.area: release cache / rollback correctness (Claude Code marketplace cache)
runtime.claim: Rehearsed and confirmed: Claude Code caches the plugin bundle by version number. Pushing new content under the same version is a no-op; rolling back by writing an older version number serves the old cached bundle, not the new tree. ADR-0013 never defines mode:rollback, so a rollback run has no defined version-number rule and will serve stale content at runtime for every Claude Code user, not just at release time.
runtime.evidence: RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md section 1 row 2 and section 2 ("Claude Code cache: confirmed live").
runtime.fix: plan.mjs must always emit a version higher than the current release head, even in rollback mode; release.yml fails the run if new version <= current head (already proposed in RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md).

runtime.area: FTS index / DB contention under single shared context.db
runtime.claim: ADR-0002 moves every session/worktree/agent of a project onto one context.db with no corruption policy. Under concurrent write load (multiple agents, multiple sessions) this is the one DB contention point for the whole project; the only existing recovery rule (PRD:84, "--fix deletes only that session DB") now deletes every session under the shared model, and names a CLI (context-mode doctor --fix) that ADR-0002 says does not exist.
runtime.evidence: REVIEW-r2.md ADR-0002:17 blocker row; open issue #867 (mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT) cited with no rule.
runtime.fix: Add a corruption section: detect at open and mid-session, hard error with a ctx_doctor fix step (tool, not CLI) that renames context.db/-wal/-shm to .corrupt-<ts> instead of deleting the shared DB.

delivery.area: critical path blocker: test layer / ADR-0003 undefined (blocks M-whatever gates v1 test pass + E2E)
delivery.claim: ADR-0003 still says v1 unit tests are deleted, against the owner decision that v1 unit tests stay until v2 passes the kept ones. 136 of 210 v1 test files import src/ directly, so every other workstream that touches src/ paths is blocked on this ADR being rewritten with a KEEP-PASS/PORT/RETIRED ledger (TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md already has the ledger: 131 KEEP-PASS, 52 PORT, 26 RETIRED) before it can call itself done, and release cannot gate on tests that do not exist yet.
delivery.evidence: REVIEW-r2.md ADR-0003:1 and :22 blockers; TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md totals and QA blocker row ("ADR-0003 names no third layer... 136/210 v1 tests import src/ directly").
delivery.fix: Adopt the TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md ledger as ADR-0003 r2 text now (already drafted in that file); this single edit unblocks every workstream gated on "tests pass" instead of leaving it as an open question.

delivery.area: owner-only step: release/CI decisions (workflow_dispatch vs tag, runner choice) sit on one doc set with contradictions
delivery.claim: ADR-0011 and ADR-0013 disagree on the release trigger (tag vs workflow_dispatch only); TECH-SPEC and ADR-0010/0011 disagree on "latest release tag" vs "latest release commit"; TECH-SPEC says runner=node:test but kept v1 tests run on vitest+TS. Each of these is a one-line pick, but none can be picked by a sub-team — they are release-pipeline decisions that gate the /release skill and CI, so they sit on the owner's desk and block everything downstream of release until resolved.
delivery.evidence: RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md section 5; TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md QA major row on dual runners.
delivery.fix: Pick workflow_dispatch-only and "commit" everywhere in one pass across ADR-0010/0011/0013/TECH-SPEC; keep both node:test and vitest in CI (already the de facto state) and say so in TECH-SPEC.

delivery.area: item blocking the most downstream work: ADR-0008 enforcement scope gaps (curl/wget, deny message, ParseError fail-open)
delivery.claim: Four separate ADR-0008 gaps (ctx-tool deny scope, curl/wget stderr flood regression of #166, dropped network-access deny text, ParseError fail-open on user deny rules) each touch the enforcement path that every other hook and formatter calls, so each is a single point that many PORT-tagged tests (ADR-0008 r3 tag, heaviest cluster per TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md) depend on before they can be written.
delivery.evidence: REVIEW-r2.md ADR-0008:16/:25/:38/:51 blockers; TEST-TRIAGE-r2.md PORT cluster note "mostly tagged ADR-0008 r3".
delivery.fix: Resolve all four ADR-0008 rows in one pass (scope table, stderr check, deny text, ParseError split) since the PORT test cluster cannot be written against a moving target.

decisions.area: Codex install mode contradiction blocks README, ADR-0011, ADR-0013, PRD alignment and the release smoke job
decisions.claim: README/ADR-0011/ADR-0013 say Codex installs as a plugin via marketplace --ref release; PRD E25 says Codex installs as a plain config.toml MCP entry with no automatic project source. This single open question blocks: the release smoke job (which file to check), the v1->v2 migration order (section 4 of RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md), and the Codex row of the detect table (ADR-0011 footprint gaps).
decisions.evidence: REVIEW-r2.md README.md:52; RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md section 1 row 1 and section 3 Codex row.
decisions.fix: Pick plugin mode (it is what is rehearsed and partially working per RELEASE-AND-MIGRATION-r2.md section 2); then fix the Codex marketplace ref gap in the same pass (ADR-0011:31).

decisions.area: AI-agent-only issue intake has no enforcement path — open question blocking owner's explicit rule
decisions.claim: Owner rule: issue templates must target AI agents exclusively, and an agent reading them must comply and send maximum debug data. ADR-0014 designs intake as a web form only; coding agents file via gh issue create --body-file or REST POST /issues, where the web form's required-field enforcement does not apply. No workflow currently validates issue bodies or recomputes the report digest, so nothing blocks a low-debug-data issue from an agent today. This is an open decision (web-form-only vs. machine-readable spec) blocking the entire issue-intake system from meeting the owner's rule.
decisions.fix: Add .github/AGENT_ISSUE.md with the same fixed ### headings as the web form (machine-readable for agents) plus .github/workflows/issue-intake.yml that re-splits the body and checks the digest, rejecting bodies that skip required debug fields.

decisions.area: needs-decision issue backlog (71 open, 12 unverdicted) has no owner triage order
decisions.claim: 71 of 269 triaged issues are needs-decision and 12 carry no verdict at all; several (e.g. #1261 hook CPU budget, #1258 ZCode/agent-removal scope, #1279 OpenCode 2 compact timing) gate GS6/GP3/ADR-0009 work directly. Without a single ranked list, each dependent workstream re-derives its own priority.
decisions.evidence: ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2.md totals table and sample rows #1261, #1258, #1279, #1271.
decisions.fix: Owner picks one ranked batch of needs-decision issues per milestone instead of resolving them ad hoc inside unrelated ADRs; start with the three that already have a proposed answer in the Rows table (#1261, #1258, #1271).

release_and_migration_risks: Codex marketplace never follows the release ref (blocker, ADR-0011:31) — existing Codex installs silently stay on main forever.
Claude Code rollback serves stale cache because mode:rollback is undefined (blocker) — any rollback attempt during an incident makes the incident worse, not better.
Smoke test runs after publish, not before (major) — a broken release is already live before smoke fails; fix is staging-ref-then-fast-forward.

v1 footprint detect table misses: Gemini/Qwen/Kiro/Copilot-CLI/VS Code MCP entries, ~/.context-mode/platform.json (API key, must never be deleted), 3 of 4 /tmp/context-mode-* prefixes (one is a live-session ready-sentinel — deleting it while v1 runs breaks that session), and the Codex marketplace/plugins TOML entries.

ADR-0011's current migration step order removes the npm global install before cleanup, which the doc itself admits breaks Copilot CLI/VS Code/Codex hooks mid-migration; safe order is install v2 -> restart -> ctx_upgrade -> restart -> ctx_doctor clean -> npm uninstall last.
Two concurrent release runs can pick the same version and race on push (minor) — needs concurrency: {group: release} and --force-with-lease.
